gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Futuristic and tech-minded, Audiowide sets its tile-like glyphs with wide gaps and no swelling in the bowls. And Noto Sans Syriac is the soft counterweight, with tall rounded lowercase like blown glass bulbs and easy s turns.

gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wester: Audiowide's strokes look like twine pressed into a flat surface, with no thick-thin shift anywhere. Noto Sans Syriac Western can take a modest size, since its terminals stay far from the stroke and its small letters feel packed with height.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-tagalo: Noto Sans Tagalog reads with a middle zone that dominates each line and generous gaps in its curves. And Almendra Display would feel cramped and fussy if shrunk down, so let it stay large and ornate.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Audiowide is all futuristic tech, its curves never thinning and its glyphs set like tiles with wide grout lines. Noto Sans Tagbanwa follows with open curves and lowercase filling most of the height, and a size near ordinary text suggests itself.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Ornate, bookish and a bit theatrical up top. Almendra Display carries all the flourish while Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes out before they touch, and that quiet restraint is what the pair does best.
gen-bebas-neue-fs-bespoke-slab: A tube-like, constant-width stroke gives Bebas Neue its clustered, commanding band of capitals. And Bespoke Slab answers in tall-bodied lowercase, grounded and refined, so the two settle into an editorial rhythm that suits a handful of lines.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-tai-vi: Ornate letters, bookish charm. Almendra Display never pinches its shapes shut, while Noto Sans Tai Viet pulls its terminals back from where the curves close, and that approachable looseness is the pair's best trait.
